findings.title: Comm scale bounds contradiction
findings.description: The paper states two mutually exclusive scale ranges for its lead predictor. The Measures section defines four response options topping out at 4 = 'Outstanding'; the Results section describes the same variable as sitting on a '1.25-5 scale'. Under the Measures reading, NO coalition can exceed 4, so the proportion above 4 is necessarily 0/64; the tool shows that is very hard to reconcile with mean 3.83 / SD 0.42 (expected 34.3% above 4, binomial p = 3.0e-12). The interpretive gloss compounds the conflict: on a 1-4 scale a mean of 3.83 sits between 'Good' and 'Outstanding', much nearer the latter, yet the text glosses it as 'good' - which reads naturally only on a 1-5 scale. I have DOWNGRADED
findings.location: Results para 1 vs Measures, Engaging communication; Table 1 Communication row

anchors.quote: Measures: 'response options 1 = Needs a lot of work, 2 = Needs a little work, 3 = Good, 4 = Outstanding; Cronbach's alpha =0.93'. Results: 'the mean level of engaging communication was 3.83 on a 1.25 -5 scale, corresponding to "good" for such facets as frequency.' Table 1: 'Communication (mean, SD) | 3.83 (0.42)'.

findings.notes: The paper states two mutually exclusive scale ranges for its lead predictor. The Measures section defines four response options topping out at 4 = 'Outstanding'; the Results section describes the same variable as sitting on a '1.25-5 scale'. Under the Measures reading, NO coalition can exceed 4, so the proportion above 4 is necessarily 0/64; the tool shows that is very hard to reconcile with mean 3.83 / SD 0.42 (expected 34.3% above 4, binomial p = 3.0e-12). The interpretive gloss compounds the conflict: on a 1-4 scale a mean of 3.83 sits between 'Good' and 'Outstanding', much nearer the latter, yet the text glosses it as 'good' - which reads naturally only on a 1-5 scale. I have DOWNGRADED the tool's own 'highly_suspicious' to 'suspicious' because the test assumes normality, and a ceiling-bounded aggregate would be left-skewed, which weakens (though does not remove) the inference. Note also that check_sd_range finds SD 0.42 admissible under BOTH readings, so dispersion alone does not resolve which scale is correct. This is a documentary contradiction between two stated constraints, not an invented bound; it warrants clarification because it changes how the headline predictor should be interpreted.

findings.title: Table2 constant p below threshold unreachable
findings.description: The z was produced by check_regression (t = B/SE = -4.51/1.50 = -3.0067), an MCP-only tool with no CLI form; statcheck then recomputed p. Reported 'p<.001' but the coefficient and its SE imply p = .0026, about 2.6x the claimed threshold. I deliberately also tested the most favourable rounding of the printed 2-dp inputs (z = 3.02), which still gives p = .0025, so the discrepancy is NOT explained by rounding - statcheck's own correct_at_printed_precision field returns false. This is an intercept, not a substantive claim, so it changes no conclusion; it is a reporting error.

findings.title: Table3 ebp baseline uninformative precision
findings.description: Columns 1 and 3 print an IDENTICAL coefficient and SE (0.01, 0.002) yet report p = .01 and p < .001 respectively - the same inputs cannot give both. At the point estimate z = 5.00 implies p = 1e-6, so the '.01' in column 1 is off by roughly four orders of magnitude and statcheck flags it. IMPORTANT COUNTERWEIGHT, which is why I hold this at 'suspicious' and not higher: the coefficient is printed to only ONE significant figure (0.01), so its rounding interval [0.005, 0.015] against an SE interval of [0.0015, 0.0025] admits z anywhere from 2.0 to 10.0, and p = .01 IS reachable inside that range. The real problem here is uninformative reported precision - as printed, this row cannot be verified

findings.title: Statcheck no decision errors (Tables 2, 3 and 4, all reconstructed z-tests)
findings.description: The single most important counterweight in this sweep. Across 24 reconstructed tests statcheck found ZERO decision errors - no p-value falls on the wrong side of .05, so not one of the paper's significance calls flips. All nine headline predictor tests (three leadership measures x three outcomes) recompute correctly from their own coefficients and standard errors, with the one exception logged separately at table3_idm_p_inconsistent, whose error runs in the conservative direction. This also CONFIRMS that the parenthesised values in Tables 2-4 are standard errors, not the SDs the column headers claim (see table_headers_mislabelled).

findings.title: Treatment assignment covariate absent (Methods, Covariates para vs Tables 2, 3 and 4)
findings.description: The Methods state explicitly that EVERY model included the randomized Check-Up assignment indicator, and the covariate list is introduced as 'apart from Coalition Check Up treatment assignment status'. No such row appears in Table 2, 3 or 4. The randomized comparison embedded in this study - half of 68 coalitions were randomly assigned to the Check-Up TA - is therefore never reported anywhere in the paper. This is a reporting gap rather than a numerical inconsistency, but it means a stated model term cannot be checked and the trial's own randomization is invisible.

findings.title: Multiplicity uncorrected (Analyses section; Tables 2-4 key predictor rows)
findings.description: Nine primary tests are run (three leadership measures x three outcomes) with no correction stated, and covariates are additionally selected by a data-driven bivariate screen at p<0.10. The five nominally significant primary results have p-values between .01 and .03; none would survive a Bonferroni-type adjustment across the nine-test family. I am flagging the ABSENCE of a stated correction, which is a design/reporting observation - it is not an arithmetic error and is entirely ordinary in this literature. The Bonferroni figure is context only and was not produced by a tool.

findings.title: Table1 members default scale artifact (Table 1, Number of coalition members row)
findings.description: RECORDED AS A NEAR-MISS FALSE ACCUSATION. On the first pass, check_table returned 'impossible' for both GRIMMER and SPRITE on this row. Inspecting the methodology strings showed why: I had declared no upper bound for coalition size, so the tools fell back to a DEFAULT 1-7 scale, on which a mean of 35.78 is trivially out of range. The granularity test had actually passed (grim_consistent: true); only the range test failed, and on an assumed bound. Re-run with a defensible bound, the row is fully GRIM- and GRIMMER-consistent and a valid integer sample exists. The paper states no maximum coalition size, so no range-based claim should be made about this row at all.

findings.title: Sprite reach search exhausted (Table 1, EBP reach row)
findings.description: EXPLICITLY NOT A FINDING. SPRITE's stochastic search failed to reconstruct a matching sample over a 0-5370 integer range, but the outcome is 'search_exhausted', not 'no_solution_proven'. Only the latter is evidence. Over a range this wide the search space is enormous and failure tells us about the search, not the data. GRIM and GRIMMER both passed on this same row inside check_table. Recorded so that the failed search is visible and cannot be mistaken for an anomaly.

findings.title: Ebp adherence cell ambiguous (Table 1, EBP adherence row)
findings.description: NO TOOL WAS RUN ON THIS CELL, by design. parse_cells_typed returned kind='ambiguous' because - alone among Table 1's continuous rows - this row label omits the '(mean, SD)' annotation that disambiguates every other one. findings.title: No apa statistics in body (Full body text)
findings.description: Run over the body text as instructed; zero APA-format statistics were found. This is a true property of the paper, not a tool failure: the narrative reports significance only as bare thresholds ('p<.05', 'p<.01') with no accompanying test statistic or df, and every verifiable number lives in the tables. It is why the NHST verification in this sweep had to be routed through coefficient/SE reconstruction instead.

findings.title: Power not reported (Analyses section (absent); Tables 2-4)
findings.description: The paper states no a-priori power analysis, so verify_power_analysis has nothing to reproduce and was not run - that absence is itself the reporting finding. For context only, required_n shows that detecting a moderate association (r = 0.30) at 80% power would need 85 units, against the 64 coalitions actually analysed. The comparison is indicative rather than exact, since the coalition-level models are Poisson and negative binomial with six covariates, not a simple correlation. The paper does invoke power informally to justify retaining zero-EBP coalitions.
